The largest possible value of ⌊N/3⌋ is 29, attained at N = 87.

Let the bag have r red, w white and b blue balls. The probability of drawing one of each color is

P = 6rwb / (N(N−1)(N−2)),

and for fixed N this is largest when r, w, b are as equal as possible. We need P > 23/100 and check each residue of N mod 3.

**Case N = 3k** (counts k, k, k):
P = 2k² / ((3k−1)(3k−2)) > 23/100.
This gives 200k² > 207k² − 207k + 46, i.e. 7k² − 207k + 46 < 0.
The upper root is (207 + √41561)/14 ≈ 29.3, so k ≤ 29.
Check k = 29: 7·841 − 207·29 + 46 = 5887 − 6003 + 46 = −70 < 0, so it works.
Check k = 30: 6300 − 6210 + 46 = 136 > 0, so it fails.
So N = 87 works, giving ⌊N/3⌋ = 29.

**Case N = 3k+1** (counts k, k, k+1):
P = 2k(k+1) / ((3k+1)(3k−1)) > 23/100.
This gives 7k² − 200k − 23 < 0, so k ≤ 28 and ⌊N/3⌋ ≤ 28.

**Case N = 3k+2** (counts k, k+1, k+1):
P = 2(k+1)² / ((3k+2)(3k+1)) > 23/100.
This gives 7k² − 193k − 154 < 0, so k ≤ 28 and ⌊N/3⌋ ≤ 28.

Larger N fails in every case, since the probability falls toward 6/27 ≈ 0.222 < 0.23 as N grows.

ANSWER: 29
